turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr. Harlan, have a seat. What's going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): My wife dragged me down here. Little cough in the mornings. It's nothing, really.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's not nothing. He coughs every morning, and he gets winded hauling groceries in from the car.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Short of breath on level ground?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Flat's fine. A hill, maybe. I'm sixty-two, come on.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the morning cough been there?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, last winter, or the one before. I don't know. I don't write this stuff down.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever? Chest pain? Any blood in the phlegm?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no, and no. Little bit of clear junk in the morning. That's normal.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You skipped the chest infection. He was wiped out.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): It was a bug. Few weeks back, three maybe. They gave me a Z-pack and I finished it. Over and done.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Azithromycin, completed. You still have the Advair, the purple one?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, it's in a drawer somewhere. I use it when I remember. Not religious about it.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Prescribed dose is 250/50, one puff twice a day. Is that what you're doing?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day? Nah. Couple times a week if the air's junk. The blue one, albuterol, two puffs if I'm really huffing. Hardly ever need it.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cigarettes. How many a day?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): About ten a day. Well, actually, maybe twenty. Depends. Not a big deal.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's smoked since he was sixteen. I've been on him to quit for years.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): The truck still needs the inspection sticker. That's the real errand after this.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ankle swelling? Any weight change?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling. Weight's the same. Can we speed this up?
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nighttime wheezing?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I sleep fine.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me listen to your chest. Scattered wheezes on both sides. I don't hear crackles. Oxygen sat is 95 percent.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Told you I'm fine.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Spirometry from this morning. FEV1 is 1.7 liters, 61 percent of predicted. FVC is 3.1 liters. The ratio is 55 percent.
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That sounds low.

[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not putting COPD in the chart today. This could be the smoking, could be leftover from that infection. I won't decide until the inhaler is actually used and we repeat the test.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): So you don't know. Great use of an afternoon.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): I know the numbers show obstruction. Use the Advair every single day, one puff in the morning and one at night. Albuterol two puffs only when you're short of breath, then sit down.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh-huh.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm also sending a referral to the smoking cessation program. They handle the patches and the coaching.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't want a patch. Twenty isn't some emergency.
[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Send it anyway. I'll get him there.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Already sent. Follow up here in six weeks for repeat spirometry. If the breathing gets worse, or you see blood, come in sooner and don't wait out the six weeks.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks. Fine. We good?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): We're good. Grab the referral printout at the desk on your way out.
